It's all pretty easy except for when you run in to rust or a previous guy's hack job, or you break something, or find deeper problems, find your tool wont work as expected, etc. That stuff just takes experience.

Simply trying to get the rusted rotors if the hubs to pull the CV axles for example. Or finding it's attached with some weird japanese quasi-philips screws and you strip the heads so then have to drill them out or try an extractor. Sometimes youre lucky and they make it easy by having holes you can drive bolts through to crack it off the hub.

It depends on your knowledge level. It can help with terminology and general concepts, but it does simplify things. The cars in the game will not be an replica of your vehicle. If you are someone who looks up forum post how-to guides and youtube videos for your particular vehicle to try and figure out if you can do a job or if it's too complicated and you need to pay someone else, then it can help you make sense of the information you're coming across in your research. In the game you never have to replace gaskets or have anything machined but it's crucial to do that irl. If you're researching what youre doing well enough before you do it then you should learn when that shit is needed that way.

The reality of working on cars is that the difficult part of the actual work is getting the tasks done with the tools you have. One of the most unrealistic things about the game is that when you want to unscrew something you just click on the bolt for a second while it unspins itself. In the real world, shops torque the fuck out of bolts and nuts with their industrial strength air compressor and impact wrench, then the car gets driven around for years getting dirty and rusted up a bit, then you come along with your hand tools and penetrating fluid and have to have the patience, strength, and tools to get all those things apart. Knowing how to replace your brake pads doesnt help you if you're going to spend an hour trying to get the wheels off with the oem lug wrench then give up because you were only able to crack a few of them.

Which is why when I had my new tires balanced I told them not to overtighten the damn things. Hand tools worked well for decades.

And yeah, having the right tools is half the battle.
